Below is a 12‑week strength program starting 2026-06-01, phased around a predictable 28‑day cycle with severe dysmenorrhea days 1–3. It honors: no high‑intensity work, no heavy Valsalva lifting, and no jumping on cycle days 1–3. Outside that window, she’s fully cleared. The plan advances strength across mesocycles while tapering load around menses so she can keep progressing month to month.

Key calendar anchors (based on LMP 2026-05-01, 28‑day cycle):
- Cycle 1: 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-28
- Cycle 2: 2026-05-29 to 2026-06-25 → Flow days: Jun 1–3 (Cycle Day 4 on Jun 2? Note: with 28-day cycle from May 29, Day 1 = May 29; however, client reports last period May 1. For simplicity, we’ll set expected menses start dates every 28 days from 2026-05-29: 2026-05-29, 2026-06-26, 2026-07-24. Many clients track by symptoms; use these as targets and adjust one or two days as needed.)
- Practical flow windows in this plan:
  - Flow Window A: 2026-06-26 to 2026-06-28 (Cycle 3, Days 1–3)
  - Flow Window B: 2026-07-24 to 2026-07-26 (Cycle 4, Days 1–3)
  - There is no flow window during June 1–25 in this 12‑week block; she is post‑menses and in follicular/ovulatory/luteal phases for most of June.

Structure overview
- Frequency: 4 strength days/week + 1 optional low‑intensity cardio/restore day.
- Sessions: ~60–70 minutes on strength days; ~30–40 minutes on restore day.
- Progression: 3 phases of 4 weeks each. Each 4‑week block has: Week 1 build, Week 2 build, Week 3 peak, Week 4 deload (aligned as closely as possible to menses; the Jul deload coincides exactly, the Jun deload is a normal training week).
- Intensity language:
  - RPE: effort out of 10. Avoid Valsalva—cue continuous or 1:1 tempo breathing on all sets; exhale through exertion.
  - No jumps/plyometrics on flow days; substitute mobility/activation and light tempo work.
- Big lifts: squat, hinge, push, pull variants. We will bias volume earlier follicular (generally higher recovery) and taper around menses and mid‑luteal if needed.
- Warm‑ups every session: 6–8 minutes easy cardio nasal breathing + mobility (T‑spine openers, 90/90 hips, cat‑cow), then movement‑specific ramp sets.

Phase goals
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4: Jun 1–28): Technical foundation and volume base; 6–10 reps, moderate load.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8: Jun 29–Jul 26): Strength emphasis; 4–6 reps on primaries; deload aligns with Jul 24–26 flow days.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12: Jul 27–Aug 23): Intensification to 3–5 reps on primaries; controlled volume; final week includes a mini‑taper/test (no maxing; submax sets) and coincides just after menses, leveraging higher capacity.

General recovery and dysmenorrhea support
- On flow days (Days 1–3): prioritize heat (heating pad pre/post), gentle diaphragmatic breathing (box breathing 4‑4‑4‑4, 5 minutes), light walking, and mobility. Hydration with electrolytes; avoid NSAIDs unless prescribed by GP.
- Sleep: target 7.5–9 hours; luteal phase may need +30–60 minutes.
- Nutrition: protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; carbs 3–5 g/kg/day baseline. In late luteal (5–7 days pre‑menses), add ~200 kcal/day mostly from complex carbs and omega‑3 sources; magnesium glycinate 300–400 mg nightly may help cramps (confirm with GP). Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day steady.
- Menstrual‑safe breathing: exhale on exertion; avoid prolonged bracing/straining. Keep reps in reserve (RIR) ≥2 on flow days.

Weekly template codes
- S1: Lower focus (squat dominant)
- S2: Upper push/pull
- S3: Lower focus (hinge dominant)
- S4: Upper push/pull + accessories
- Optional R: Restore/Zone‑2 cardio + mobility

Exercises key (use barbell or dumbbell/machine as available; swap like‑for‑like if needed)
- Squat: Back Squat or Goblet/Front Squat
- Hinge: Romanian Deadlift (RDL), Trap‑bar Deadlift, Hip Thrust
- Push: Bench Press or DB Bench, Overhead Press (OHP) or DB OHP
- Pull: One‑Arm DB Row, Lat Pulldown or Pull‑ups, Seated Row
- Single‑leg: Split Squat/Reverse Lunge, Step‑up
- Core: Pallof Press, Dead Bug, Side Plank, Farmer Carry
- Conditioning finishers only outside flow days; otherwise replace with breathing/mobility.

PHASE 1 — Weeks 1–4 (Jun 1–28): Build technical base, volume, work capacity
Intensity: RPE 6–8 on main lifts, 2–3 RIR. Rest 90–150s on compounds, 60–90s on accessories.

Week 1 (Jun 1–7)
- S1 (Lower Squat): Back Squat 4x6 @RPE7; Split Squat 3x8/side; RDL 3x8; Leg Curl 3x12; Calf Raise 3x12; Core: Dead Bug 3x8/side
- S2 (Upper): DB Bench 4x8 @RPE7; One‑Arm DB Row 4x8/side; OHP 3x8; Lat Pulldown 3x10; Face Pull 3x12; Core: Pallof 3x10/side
- S3 (Lower Hinge): Trap‑bar Deadlift 4x5 @RPE7; Front Squat or Goblet 3x8; Hip Thrust 3x10; Hamstring Slideouts 3x10; Core: Side Plank 3x30–45s/side
- S4 (Upper/Accessories): Incline DB Bench 3x10; Seated Cable Row 3x10; Arnold Press 3x10; Pullover 3x12; Curl 3x12; Triceps Rope 3x12; Farmer Carry 4x20–30m
- Optional R: 30–40 min Zone‑2 cardio + 10 min mobility

Week 2 (Jun 8–14)
- Progress loads +2.5–5% where RPE ≤7 last week
- S1: Back Squat 5x6 @RPE7–8; Split Squat 3x10; RDL 4x8; Leg Curl 3x12; Calf 3x15; Dead Bug 3x10/side
- S2: DB Bench 4x8–9 @RPE7–8; One‑Arm Row 4x8–9; OHP 4x6–8; Lat Pulldown 4x8–10; Face Pull 3x12–15; Pallof 3x12/side
- S3: Trap‑bar Deadlift 5x4–5 @RPE7–8; Front/Goblet 3x8–10; Hip Thrust 4x8–10; Ham Slideouts 3x12; Side Plank 3x45s
- S4: Similar to Week 1; aim small load/reps up

Week 3 (Jun 15–21) — Peak of Phase 1
- S1: Back Squat 4x6 @RPE8; Split Squat 4x8; RDL 4x8; Leg Curl 3x12–15; Dead Bug 3x10–12/side
- S2: Bench (BB or DB) 5x6–8 @RPE8; One‑Arm Row 4x8; OHP 4x6; Pull‑ups or Lat PD 4x6–8 heavier; Face Pull 3x15; Pallof 3x12–15
- S3: Trap‑bar Deadlift 4x4 @RPE8; Front/Goblet 3x8; Hip Thrust 4x8 heavy; Ham Slideouts 3x12–15; Side Plank 3x45–60s
- S4: Keep volume; push small loads if RPE allows

Week 4 (Jun 22–28) — Deload volume, keep movement quality
- All main lifts: 3x5–6 @RPE6 (about 80–85% of Week 3 loads)
- Accessories: 2 sets each, keep form, stop 3 RIR
- Core and carries light
- No conditioning finishers; keep Zone‑2 only

PHASE 2 — Weeks 5–8 (Jun 29–Jul 26): Strength emphasis; deload aligns with menses (Jul 24–26)
Shift to lower reps on primaries. Maintain strict exhale on effort to avoid heavy bracing.

Week 5 (Jun 29–Jul 5)
- S1: Back Squat 5x4–5 @RPE7–8; Split Squat 3x8; RDL 4x6–8; Leg Curl 3x10–12; Dead Bug 3x10/side
- S2: Bench Press 5x4–6 @RPE7–8; One‑Arm Row 4x8; OHP 4x5–6; Lat PD 4x6–8; Pallof 3x12/side
- S3: Trap‑bar Deadlift 5x3–4 @RPE7–8; Front/Goblet 3x6–8; Hip Thrust 4x6–8; Ham Slideouts 3x10–12; Side Plank 3x45–60s
- S4: Incline DB Bench 4x8; Seated Row 4x8; Arnold Press 3x8–10; Pullover 3x10–12; Curl 3x10–12; Triceps 3x10–12; Farmer Carry 4x25–30m

Week 6 (Jul 6–12)
- Progress +2.5–5% if RPE last week ≤7.5
- S1: Back Squat 5x4 @RPE8; Split Squat 3x8–10; RDL 4x6–8; Leg Curl 3x12
- S2: Bench 5x4–5 @RPE8; Row 4x8; OHP 4x5; Lat PD 4x6–8; Face Pull 3x12–15
- S3: Trap‑bar Deadlift 5x3–4 @RPE8; Front/Goblet 3x6–8; Hip Thrust 4x6–8 heavy; Ham Slideouts 3x12
- S4: Similar to Week 5; small progression

Week 7 (Jul 13–19) — Peak of Phase 2
- S1: Back Squat 4x4 @RPE8–8.5; RDL 4x6; Split Squat 3x8; Core as prior
- S2: Bench 4x4 @RPE8–8.5; Row 4x8; OHP 4x4–5; Lat PD 4x6; Accessories moderate
- S3: Trap‑bar Deadlift 4x3 @RPE8–8.5; Front/Goblet 3x6; Hip Thrust 4x6; Core steady
- S4: Keep volume, don’t chase fatigue

Week 8 (Jul 20–26) — Deload coinciding with flow days Jul 24–26
- Jul 20–23 (pre‑flow): Reduce to 3x3–5 @RPE6–6.5 on primaries; accessories 2x10 easy
- Jul 24–26 (Flow Days 1–3): No high intensity, no heavy bracing, no jumping
  - Replace sessions with:
    - 20–30 min easy walk or cycle (RPE 3–4)
    - 10–15 min mobility: pelvic tilts, 90/90, child’s pose, cat‑cow, low‑tension hip flexor stretch
    - 2–3 light activation circuits (no strain): Glute Bridge 2x12 (exhale up), Band Pull‑Apart 2x15, Dead Bug 2x6/side, Pallof Hold 2x20s/side
  - If cramping is severe, skip or do breathing + heat only

PHASE 3 — Weeks 9–12 (Jul 27–Aug 23): Intensify to 3–5 reps; controlled volume; submax “test”
We capitalize on early follicular/early‑mid cycle after the Jul flow window to push strength, then manage fatigue late luteal. Next expected menses around Aug 21–23; we’ll taper slightly in Week 12 to avoid straining if it begins.

Week 9 (Jul 27–Aug 2)
- S1: Back Squat 5x3–4 @RPE7.5–8; Split Squat 3x6–8; RDL 4x5–6
- S2: Bench 5x3–4 @RPE7.5–8; Row 4x6–8; OHP 4x3–5; Lat PD 4x6
- S3: Trap‑bar Deadlift 5x2–3 @RPE7.5–8; Front Squat/Goblet 3x5–6; Hip Thrust 4x5–6
- S4: Incline DB Bench 3x8; Seated Row 3x8; Accessory tri/bi 2–3x10–12; Carries 3–4x30m

Week 10 (Aug 3–9) — Peak loading for block
- S1: Back Squat 4x3 @RPE8–8.5; RDL 4x5; Split Squat 3x6–8
- S2: Bench 4x3 @RPE8–8.5; OHP 4x3–4; Row 4x6; Lat PD 3x6–8
- S3: Trap‑bar Deadlift 4x2–3 @RPE8–8.5; Hip Thrust 4x5; Front/Goblet 3x5
- S4: Accessories moderate; don’t exceed RPE8

Week 11 (Aug 10–16) — Slight taper, keep sharpness
- S1: Back Squat 3x3 @RPE7–7.5; Then 1 top AMRAP set leaving 2 RIR (capped at RPE8) at same load for reps PR
- S2: Bench 3x3 @RPE7–7.5; Then AMRAP 1 set @2 RIR; Rows/OHP light 2–3x6–8
- S3: Trap‑bar Deadlift 3x2–3 @RPE7–7.5; Then AMRAP 1 set @2 RIR; Hip Thrust 3x5–6 easy
- S4: Light accessories 2x10–12; mobility emphasis

Week 12 (Aug 17–23) — Consolidate; anticipate menses ~Aug 21–23
- Aug 17–20: Technique doubles/triples @RPE6–6.5 on primaries (3x2–3 each); Accessories 2x8–10
- Aug 21–23 (if flow starts): Follow flow‑day protocol (gentle walk, mobility, activation). If period hasn’t started, keep sessions easy and avoid grinders or breath‑holding.

Session format details
- Warm‑up (all days): 5 min easy cardio; T‑spine rotation 2x6/side; 90/90 hip flow 2x6/side; Cat‑cow 10 reps; Breathing primer: 4 breaths with long exhale.
- Movement prep: 2–3 ramp sets for first lift (e.g., 5 @50%, 3 @65%, 1 @75% of day’s working load).
- Tempo/breathing: 2–3 second controlled eccentric; exhale on concentric. No prolonged valsalva; brief brace only if symptom‑free and outside flow days, but still cue exhale through sticking point.
- Cool‑down: 5–8 min easy cardio + light stretching; optional heat application in late luteal/flow.

Load selection and progression
- Start Week 1 using estimated 1RMs from recent training or conservative guesses. Aim RPE targets first; add 2.5–5% weekly when you finish with ≥2 reps in reserve and no symptom flare.
- If cramps, pelvic pressure, or low‑back sensitivity increase: reduce load 5–10%, cut a set, or switch to machine/db variation that feels more supportive (e.g., hack squat, leg press, chest‑supported row).
- Maintain 1–2 RIR on all sets during luteal days 21–28 of each cycle; push closer to 0–1 RIR only in nominated peak weeks outside flow days.

Conditioning guidance
- Outside flow days: optional 1–2 short finishers per week (e.g., 6–8 min EMOM of moderate sled push, bike sprints 10s on/50s off x 8). Skip during luteal days if recovery dips.
- Flow days: no HIIT; stick to easy zone‑2 or walking.

Cycle‑phase notes for coaching
- Early follicular (post‑flow): often best window for progression; schedule rep PRs and heavier triples here (Weeks 9–10 exploit this).
- Ovulatory: watch for joint laxity; emphasize bracing cues and controlled eccentrics.
- Luteal: slightly longer warm‑ups, more hydration/electrolytes; cap RPE at 8; extend rest 15–30s.

What to track weekly
- RPEs on primary lifts, cramps score 0–10, pelvic pressure 0–10, energy, sleep hours, and period dates. Adjust the exact flow‑day substitutions by actual start date if it shifts.

Summary of flow‑day accommodations within the 12 weeks
- Jun: No flow days inside the June 1–28 window; normal training with a deload in Week 4.
- Jul 24–26: Full flow protocol and deload in Week 8.
- Late Aug (Week 12): Likely onset; sessions already dialed back; switch to flow protocol upon start.

This structure keeps her progressing monthly while protecting her during the most symptomatic days, aligning peak strength work right after menses and easing off as the next cycle begins.
